# Key terms
- Absolute reference: A cell reference fixed with $, such as $A$1, which doesn't change when the formula is copied (https://getgradify.com/terms/absolute-reference/)
- Absolute risk: The probability of an event in a group over a stated period (https://getgradify.com/terms/absolute-risk/)
- Abstract: A short summary of a paper (https://getgradify.com/terms/abstract/)
- Accountability: Being answerable for your actions and omissions and able to justify them (https://getgradify.com/terms/accountability/)
- Active listening: Listening with full attention, reflecting back and checking understanding (https://getgradify.com/terms/active-listening/)
- Active transport: Movement across a membrane against a concentration gradient, using energy from ATP (https://getgradify.com/terms/active-transport/)
- Acute kidney injury: A rapid reduction in kidney function over hours to days (https://getgradify.com/terms/acute-kidney-injury/)
- Adaptation: An inherited feature that increases survival and reproduction (https://getgradify.com/terms/adaptation/)
- Advance decision to refuse treatment: A legally binding refusal of specified treatment made while the person has capacity (https://getgradify.com/terms/advance-decision-to-refuse-treatment/)
- Adverse childhood experiences: Stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect (https://getgradify.com/terms/adverse-childhood-experiences/)
- Agent: The party who acts on behalf of the principal (https://getgradify.com/terms/agent/)
- Alt text: A short text alternative for an image, read by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load (https://getgradify.com/terms/alt-text/)
- Anachronism: Placing something in the wrong period, or judging the past by later assumptions (https://getgradify.com/terms/anachronism/)
- Anaphylaxis: A severe, whole-body type I reaction (https://getgradify.com/terms/anaphylaxis/)
- Annotation: Written notes alongside drawings and studies that explain observations, intentions and decisions (https://getgradify.com/terms/annotation/)
- Anorexia nervosa: An eating disorder involving restriction, low weight and intense fear of weight gain (https://getgradify.com/terms/anorexia-nervosa/)
- Anticholinergic burden: The cumulative effect of medicines with anticholinergic properties (https://getgradify.com/terms/anticholinergic-burden/)
- Anticipatory medicines: Medicines prescribed in advance to manage expected symptoms at the end of life (https://getgradify.com/terms/anticipatory-medicines/)
- Antigen: A molecule, such as a cell surface marker, recognised by the immune system (https://getgradify.com/terms/antigen/)
- Antimicrobial resistance: The ability of microbes to survive drugs designed to kill them (https://getgradify.com/terms/antimicrobial-resistance/)
- Antimicrobial stewardship: Coordinated action to use antimicrobials only when needed, to limit resistance (https://getgradify.com/terms/antimicrobial-stewardship/)
- Assent: A child's agreement to care when they can't legally consent (https://getgradify.com/terms/assent/)
- Asymptote: A straight line that branches of the locus approach as gain becomes very large (https://getgradify.com/terms/asymptote/)
- Attrition: Wear from tooth-to-tooth contact (https://getgradify.com/terms/attrition/)
- Automaticity: Performing a behaviour with little conscious thought (https://getgradify.com/terms/automaticity/)
- Autonomy: Respect for people's right to make their own decisions (https://getgradify.com/terms/autonomy/)
- Baseline: The pencil line where samples are spotted (https://getgradify.com/terms/baseline/)
- Best interests: Decisions made for someone who lacks capacity based on their wishes, beliefs and welfare (https://getgradify.com/terms/best-interests/)
- Beta: A measure of a share's systematic risk relative to the market (https://getgradify.com/terms/beta/)
- Bias: A systematic error that leads to a wrong estimate of an association (https://getgradify.com/terms/bias/)
- Bioavailability: The fraction of an administered dose that reaches the systemic circulation unchanged (https://getgradify.com/terms/bioavailability/)
- Biopsychosocial model: Engel's (1977) model in which health results from interacting biological, psychological and social factors (https://getgradify.com/terms/biopsychosocial-model/)
- Body mass index: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared (https://getgradify.com/terms/body-mass-index/)
- Bolam test: Acting in accordance with a responsible body of professional opinion (https://getgradify.com/terms/bolam-test/)
- Buffer: A solution that resists changes in pH (https://getgradify.com/terms/buffer/)
- Burnout: An occupational phenomenon of exhaustion, cynicism and reduced efficacy from unmanaged chronic work stress (https://getgradify.com/terms/burnout/)
- Caldicott Guardian: A senior person responsible for protecting the confidentiality of people's information in an organisation (https://getgradify.com/terms/caldicott-guardian/)
- Canon: The works and artists regarded as the most important in a tradition (https://getgradify.com/terms/canon/)
- Capacity: The ability to understand, retain, weigh information and communicate a decision (https://getgradify.com/terms/capacity/)
- Cardiac output: The volume of blood pumped by one ventricle per minute; heart rate × stroke volume (https://getgradify.com/terms/cardiac-output/)
- Case study: A structured account of one project from problem to outcome (https://getgradify.com/terms/case-study/)
- Cellulitis: A spreading infection of soft tissue (https://getgradify.com/terms/cellulitis/)
- Census: An official count of the population, taken every ten years from 1801 (https://getgradify.com/terms/census/)
- Centile: A position on a growth chart showing how a child compares with others of the same age (https://getgradify.com/terms/centile/)
- Circular economy: A system that keeps materials in use through reuse, repair and recycling (https://getgradify.com/terms/circular-economy/)
- Client money: Money a firm holds on behalf of its clients, kept separate from the firm's own money (https://getgradify.com/terms/client-money/)
- Clinical audit: Comparing practice with standards and acting to improve it (https://getgradify.com/terms/clinical-audit/)
- Clinical governance: A framework for accountability and continuous improvement of care quality (https://getgradify.com/terms/clinical-governance/)
- Close reading: Detailed analysis of a short passage to show how its language and form create meaning (https://getgradify.com/terms/close-reading/)
- Code of conduct: A set of standards of behaviour expected of members of a profession (https://getgradify.com/terms/code-of-conduct/)
- Coefficient: A number in front of a formula in an equation, giving the number of particles or moles (https://getgradify.com/terms/coefficient/)
- Collusion: A request, usually from relatives, to keep information from the patient (https://getgradify.com/terms/collusion/)
- Command word: The instruction word in a question that tells you what kind of answer is needed (https://getgradify.com/terms/command-word/)
- Compensation: The secondary respiratory or renal change that moves pH back towards normal after a primary disturbance (https://getgradify.com/terms/compensation/)
- Confidence interval: A range of plausible values for an effect (https://getgradify.com/terms/confidence-interval/)
- Confidentiality: The duty to protect personal information shared in confidence (https://getgradify.com/terms/confidentiality/)
- Confirmation bias: The tendency to notice and favour information that supports existing beliefs (https://getgradify.com/terms/confirmation-bias/)
- Conflict of interest: A situation in which personal interests could influence professional judgement (https://getgradify.com/terms/conflict-of-interest/)
- Confounder: A factor associated with both exposure and outcome, not on the causal pathway, that distorts their relationship (https://getgradify.com/terms/confounder/)
- Confounding variable: An uncontrolled variable that varies with the independent variable and could account for the result (https://getgradify.com/terms/confounding-variable/)
- Contemporaneous record: A record made at the time of the work (https://getgradify.com/terms/contemporaneous-record/)
- Context: The historical, social, cultural and personal circumstances in which a work was made and seen (https://getgradify.com/terms/context/)
- Contraction: A map T with ‖Tx − Ty‖ ≤ k‖x − y‖ for some k < 1 (https://getgradify.com/terms/contraction/)
- COPD: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (https://getgradify.com/terms/copd/)
- Correlation coefficient: A measure of the strength and direction of a linear relationship, from −1 to +1 (https://getgradify.com/terms/correlation-coefficient/)
- Correlation: A statistical association between two variables (https://getgradify.com/terms/correlation/)
- COSHH: The Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002, which govern hazardous substances at work in Great Britain (https://getgradify.com/terms/coshh/)
- Coverage: Number of reads covering each base (https://getgradify.com/terms/coverage/)
- Critical path: The longest sequence of dependent tasks, determining the project's minimum duration (https://getgradify.com/terms/critical-path/)
- Crystalloid: A solution of electrolytes in water, such as sodium chloride 0.9% or Hartmann's solution (https://getgradify.com/terms/crystalloid/)
- Cultural capital: Knowledge and tastes that bring social advantage (https://getgradify.com/terms/cultural-capital/)
- Decolonisation: The process by which colonies became independent (https://getgradify.com/terms/decolonisation/)
- Degrees of freedom: Independent ways a molecule can move (https://getgradify.com/terms/degrees-of-freedom/)
- Delegation: Giving a subordinate authority to make a decision while the manager retains responsibility (https://getgradify.com/terms/delegation/)
- Deprescribing: The planned and supervised reduction or stopping of medicines that may no longer be beneficial (https://getgradify.com/terms/deprescribing/)
- Derivative claim: A claim brought by a shareholder on behalf of the company for a wrong done to it (https://getgradify.com/terms/derivative-claim/)
- Derivative: A product made to help identify a compound (https://getgradify.com/terms/derivative/)
- Designated safeguarding lead: The named person in an organisation who advises on and coordinates safeguarding concerns (https://getgradify.com/terms/designated-safeguarding-lead/)
- Desirable difficulty: A learning condition that feels harder but improves long-term retention (https://getgradify.com/terms/desirable-difficulty/)
- Devolution: The transfer of powers from the UK Parliament to the governments of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (https://getgradify.com/terms/devolution/)
- Diabetic ketoacidosis: A dangerous build-up of ketones due to lack of insulin (https://getgradify.com/terms/diabetic-ketoacidosis/)
- Diffusion: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration (https://getgradify.com/terms/diffusion/)
- Digital exclusion: Being unable to use digital services because of lack of access, skills or confidence (https://getgradify.com/terms/digital-exclusion/)
- Discourse: A system of statements and practices that constructs objects and subjects (https://getgradify.com/terms/discourse/)
- Displacement: Position relative to a chosen origin, with direction (https://getgradify.com/terms/displacement/)
- Diversification: Growth through new products in new markets (https://getgradify.com/terms/diversification/)
- Domain: The highest rank of classification: Bacteria, Archaea or Eukarya (https://getgradify.com/terms/domain/)
- Drift: The change in a portfolio's allocation caused by different returns on its assets (https://getgradify.com/terms/drift/)
- Duty of candour: The duty to be open and honest with patients when things go wrong (https://getgradify.com/terms/duty-of-candour/)
- Duty of care: A legal duty on anyone handling waste to keep it safe and pass it only to authorised persons (https://getgradify.com/terms/duty-of-care/)
- Eatwell Guide: The UK's visual model of a healthy, balanced diet for people aged 2 and over (https://getgradify.com/terms/eatwell-guide/)
- Ecosystem: A community of organisms together with their physical environment (https://getgradify.com/terms/ecosystem/)
- Effect size: The magnitude of a difference or relationship (https://getgradify.com/terms/effect-size/)
- eGFR: Estimated glomerular filtration rate calculated from serum creatinine, age and sex, valid only when function is stable (https://getgradify.com/terms/egfr/)
- EHC plan: An education, health and care plan for a child or young person with special educational needs (England) (https://getgradify.com/terms/ehc-plan/)
- Emergence: Behaviour of a whole system that arises from interactions between its parts (https://getgradify.com/terms/emergence/)
- Entropy: The tendency towards disorder and decay, an idea important to Smithson (https://getgradify.com/terms/entropy/)
- Epigenetics: Heritable changes in gene expression without sequence change (https://getgradify.com/terms/epigenetics/)
- Equity: The owners' residual interest: assets minus liabilities (https://getgradify.com/terms/equity/)
- Evaluation: Judging the significance or effectiveness of a point (https://getgradify.com/terms/evaluation/)
- Evaporation: Escape of particles from a liquid surface (https://getgradify.com/terms/evaporation/)
- Expression: A combination of numbers, letters and operations, with no equals sign, such as 3a + 2b (https://getgradify.com/terms/expression/)
- Exudate: Protein-rich extravascular fluid produced by increased vascular permeability in inflammation (https://getgradify.com/terms/exudate/)
- Feedback: Information from an employer about how you performed and could improve (https://getgradify.com/terms/feedback/)
- Field experiment: An experiment in a natural setting in which the researcher manipulates the IV (https://getgradify.com/terms/field-experiment/)
- Fingertip unit: A measure of topical steroid cream for dosing (https://getgradify.com/terms/fingertip-unit/)
- First-pass metabolism: Metabolism of a drug in the gut wall and liver before it reaches the circulation (https://getgradify.com/terms/first-pass-metabolism/)
- Fitness to practise: Having the skills, knowledge, health and character to practise safely (https://getgradify.com/terms/fitness-to-practise/)
- Fluency: The number of relevant responses produced in a divergent thinking task (https://getgradify.com/terms/fluency/)
- Forgetting curve: The pattern, first shown by Ebbinghaus, in which memory drops quickly after learning and then more slowly (https://getgradify.com/terms/forgetting-curve/)
- Formative assessment: Assessment during learning used to guide teaching (https://getgradify.com/terms/formative-assessment/)
- Forward contract: An agreement to exchange currency at a fixed rate in the future (https://getgradify.com/terms/forward-contract/)
- Fragility fracture: A fracture from a fall from standing height or less (https://getgradify.com/terms/fragility-fracture/)
- Frailty: A state of reduced reserve that makes a person vulnerable to decline after minor stress (https://getgradify.com/terms/frailty/)
- Frame narrative: A story told within another story (https://getgradify.com/terms/frame-narrative/)
- Function: A rule assigning exactly one output to each input in its domain, written f(x) or f: x ↦ … (https://getgradify.com/terms/function/)
- Functionalism: Design based mainly on purpose and use rather than decoration (https://getgradify.com/terms/functionalism/)
- Generative AI: AI that produces new content such as text, images or code (https://getgradify.com/terms/generative-ai/)
- Gillick competence: Ability of a child under 16 to consent to treatment they fully understand (https://getgradify.com/terms/gillick-competence/)
- Global warming potential: Warming effect of a gas relative to CO₂ (https://getgradify.com/terms/global-warming-potential/)
- Globalisation: The increasing integration of economies through trade, investment, technology and the movement of people (https://getgradify.com/terms/globalisation/)
- Grade: The rate of progression and risk, A to C, based on bone loss for age and modified by smoking and diabetes (https://getgradify.com/terms/grade/)
- Gradient: The change in y divided by the change in x; on a graph of amount against time it is the rate (https://getgradify.com/terms/gradient/)
- Gram stain: A staining method that separates bacteria into Gram-positive (purple) and Gram-negative (pink) by their wall structure (https://getgradify.com/terms/gram-stain/)
- Greenwashing: Misleading claims that a product is environmentally friendly (https://getgradify.com/terms/greenwashing/)
- Grey literature: Material such as reports and theses published outside commercial journals (https://getgradify.com/terms/grey-literature/)
- Habit: A behaviour triggered automatically by a context cue, learned through repetition (https://getgradify.com/terms/habit/)
- Habitus: Bourdieu's term for the dispositions people acquire from their social position, which shape what feels natural (https://getgradify.com/terms/habitus/)
- Half-life: The time for half the nuclei of a radioactive isotope in a sample to decay (https://getgradify.com/terms/half-life/)
- Hallucination: Plausible but false content produced by an AI model (https://getgradify.com/terms/hallucination/)
- HbA1c: Glycated haemoglobin: a measure of average blood glucose over the previous two to three months (https://getgradify.com/terms/hba1c/)
- Health promotion: The process of enabling people to increase control over, and to improve, their health (Ottawa Charter) (https://getgradify.com/terms/health-promotion/)
- Hepatic encephalopathy: Brain dysfunction caused by liver failure and portosystemic shunting (https://getgradify.com/terms/hepatic-encephalopathy/)
- Herd immunity: Indirect protection when most people are immune (https://getgradify.com/terms/herd-immunity/)
- Heritability: The proportion of variation in a trait due to genetic differences (https://getgradify.com/terms/heritability/)
- Heterogeneity: Variation in true effects between studies, measured by Cochran's Q, τ2 and I2 (https://getgradify.com/terms/heterogeneity/)
- Heuristic: A mental short cut or rule of thumb used to make decisions quickly (https://getgradify.com/terms/heuristic/)
- Hidden curriculum: The norms and values taught through the organisation of school life rather than the formal curriculum (https://getgradify.com/terms/hidden-curriculum/)
- Histogram: A graph showing the distribution of tones in an image from black to white (https://getgradify.com/terms/histogram/)
- Homeostasis: Keeping internal conditions within narrow limits despite changes outside (https://getgradify.com/terms/homeostasis/)
- Hormone: A chemical messenger carried in the blood (https://getgradify.com/terms/hormone/)
- HSE Management Standards: Six areas of work design used to manage work-related stress (https://getgradify.com/terms/hse-management-standards/)
- Human factors: The study of how people interact with systems, equipment and environments, used to design safer care (https://getgradify.com/terms/human-factors/)
- Hydrogen bond: A weak attraction between δ+ hydrogen and a lone pair on O or N (https://getgradify.com/terms/hydrogen-bond/)
- Hyperkalaemia: Raised serum potassium, above 5.5 mmol/L (https://getgradify.com/terms/hyperkalaemia/)
- Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state: An emergency of severe hyperglycaemia and dehydration without significant ketosis (https://getgradify.com/terms/hyperosmolar-hyperglycaemic-state/)
- Hypothesis: A testable, falsifiable explanation for an observation (https://getgradify.com/terms/hypothesis/)
- Identity: The ways people understand who they are and where they belong (https://getgradify.com/terms/identity/)
- Implementation intention: An if–then plan linking a specific situation to a goal-directed action (https://getgradify.com/terms/implementation-intention/)
- Implied consent: Consent shown by behaviour, such as opening the mouth for an examination (https://getgradify.com/terms/implied-consent/)
- Improper fraction: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator, such as 7/4 = 1¾ (https://getgradify.com/terms/improper-fraction/)
- Incidence: The number of new cases arising in a population at risk over a period (https://getgradify.com/terms/incidence/)
- Independent prescriber: A practitioner responsible for assessment and prescribing decisions (https://getgradify.com/terms/independent-prescriber/)
- Index: A measure of the combined performance of a defined group of securities (https://getgradify.com/terms/index/)
- Indirect discrimination: A neutral rule that disadvantages a protected group without objective justification (https://getgradify.com/terms/indirect-discrimination/)
- Inference: A conclusion reasoned from what a source says or shows (https://getgradify.com/terms/inference/)
